specimens.name: Guarded V-belt drive fragment
specimens.notes: PASS after art-direction correction: the belt and pulleys are surrounded by a substantial bolted formed-sheet top/side safety guard. The mechanism remains intentionally visible, matching the canonical E1 rule that dangerous mechanics are guarded while the operating principle remains readable.

specimens.name: Guarded roller-chain drive fragment
specimens.notes: PASS after art-direction correction: chain and sprockets are surrounded by a substantial formed-metal safety guard while remaining readable. This is guarded standardized E1 hardware, not an E0-style completely unguarded improvised transmission.

specimens.name: Industrial linear solenoid actuator
specimens.notes: PASS: isolated coil housing, straight plunger and mounting flange with no wiring.

specimens.name: Electromagnetic clutch/brake module
specimens.notes: PASS with recorded non-blocking visual ambiguity: compact axial cast module has two opposed shaft hubs, a slotted removable/service cover and simple mounting base, with no terminal box or surrounding drivetrain. It is superficially motor-like but still satisfies the corrected atomic clutch/brake contract and does not create an E0 regression.

review_method: Exact untouched 1536x1024 source re-inspected specimen-by-specimen after the user challenged the prior guard interpretation. Local exact-byte verification reconfirmed SHA-256 73b6674deab1ca86682f4311de648462bd7eff7cb7f2864b99f93f62704c9df2, 1866458 bytes and 1536x1024 dimensions. The canonical E1 ERA_DESIGN_MATRIX language explicitly requires protective guards around dangerous mechanics while the principle of operation remains visible; PR #69 corrected the machine-readable spec to that rule. Under the corrected merged spec, specimens 05/06 are guarded rather than completely exposed, and specimen 08 meets the compact axial two-hub/service-cover contract despite a recorded motor-like resemblance. The same untouched Drive file was moved from the rejected subfolder into canonical E1_1986 without replacing its bytes.

supersedes_review_at_parent.reason: Prior FAIL used an over-strict full-front-cover interpretation later corrected by merged PR #69 after user art-direction review. Git history preserves that earlier verdict.
